METHOD (2026-11-04, report of CI run 41823709461 on main a3a614f, dist/lib/evidence.js byte-identical to the report's embedded source). Each mutant was spliced into the built file at its report offsets (original text checked before the splice, the file read back after it), then a fixed battery of real CLI runs (`node dist/cli.js check ... --no-color --path .`, Node 24.22.1) was replayed on fresh copies of an `init --example` mission (request-triage) and every exit code, stdout, stderr and written file (lock, witness) was compared byte for byte with the pristine build. Probe runs per mutant: 26 to 40 CLI invocations; no mutant hung (60 s bound per call).
verdicts.argument: quoteEscapingOnly only chooses which sentence a projection drift gets; the drift is refused either way.

verdicts.evidence: Hole, measured 2026-11-04: a crash. On `unread` the pristine build refuses the seal (exit 1, "sealed evidence changed: code/reports/junit.xml"): `hashOfKind` yields the sentinel `unreadable`, and `quoteEscapingOnly` cannot read the file and returns false. With the catch block emptied, `text` stays undefined, `sealProjection(undefined)` throws, and `check` prints "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')" instead of the gate audit. The five other missions identical. Not equivalent although `undefined` is falsy: the mutant never reaches its return. Nothing kills it: the RWD-2026-0189 test makes a bytes entry unreadable, not a junit-projection one.
